evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary reports 拿 as a popular form of 拏 that later became an independent standard graph. It cites Shuowen’s analysis of 拏 as 手 plus phonetic 奴, glossed “pull/lead,” and points to Song–Yuan vernacular character records and later dictionaries. This documents the dictionary’s account; it does not establish a continuous semantic path for every later use.
evidence.title: [B01271-003] 拿 (拏) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry lists 拏 and 挐 among 拿’s variants. It reports Shuowen analyses of 拏 as 手 plus 奴 phonetic, “pull/lead,” and 挐 as 手 plus 加 phonetic, “hold.” It says later sources associate 拏 and 挐, and that 拿 became an independent standard graph. These are dictionary reports, not proof of a single uninterrupted graphic or semantic sequence.

evidence.field: A01571 拿, character-specific form and senses
evidence.text: The entry identifies the visible structure as 合 above 手 and says 拿 is not recorded in Shuowen. It cites later literary examples for taking or holding, forceful taking, apprehending, grasp/control, and prepositional uses. These examples do not give a complete chronology of either the spoken word or the graph.
evidence.title: [A01571] 拿 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The entry analyzes 拿 as 从手、合声 (手 semantic, 合 phonetic), with the basic sense “take by hand.” It cites a Song poem by Wang Zhidao and later literary examples for forceful taking, apprehending, control/grasping, and prepositional use. Its accessible entry gives no historical reconstruction comparison demonstrating 合’s proposed sound fit.

evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv; exact supplied rows for 合, 手, 奴, 拏; no 拿 row supplied
evidence.text: The supplied exact rows give 合 *kˤop and *m-kˤop (Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese), 手 *n̥uʔ, 奴 *nˤa, and 拏 *nˤra. There is no 拿 row in the supplied local readings. The 奴/拏 pair is similar in this system and is consistent with the dictionary’s reported analysis, but is not by itself proof of component identity or role. 合’s supplied forms do not make the proposed 合–拿 sound fit apparent; no same-system 拿 comparison is available here. Local data are not an external source and do not support claims beyond these exact rows.

search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected both Ministry dictionary pages and the CUHK entry. They support the reported 拏→拿 relationship, distinct Shuowen analyses for 拏 and 挐, and a competing CUHK proposal that 合 is phonetic in 拿. Tried opening the exact Commons file page and direct SVG; both were inaccessible. Commons search results were unrelated and do not verify this file.

gaps: No reliable early inscriptional form for 拿 itself was established. The Ministry dictionary says Shuowen does not record 拿 and instead reports Shuowen analyses of 拏 and 挐. Its account supports a reported later relation between 拏 and 拿 but does not trace stroke-by-stroke graphic change.

The phonetic status of 合 in 拿 remains disputed. CUHK asserts 合 is phonetic; the checked local Baxter–Sagart data lack a 拿 row for a same-system comparison. Do not present 合 as a settled phonetic component or treat the hands-together mnemonic as historical construction.

The local Baxter–Sagart data were supplied as exact rows, but no external character-specific table page was verified in this pass. Preserve their notation and local provenance; do not cite them as if externally inspected.

Later forceful-taking, control, and prepositional uses are reported, but their chronology and semantic transitions are not fully established.
